name: Blade of the Bloodchief
oracle_text:
Whenever a creature dies, put a +1/+1 counter on equipped creature. If equipped creature is a Vampire, put two +1/+1 counters on it instead.
Equip {1}
blocked_sentences: Whenever a creature dies, put a +1/+1 counter on equipped creature. If equipped creature is a Vampire, put two +1/+1 counters on it instead.

needs.what: an `attached` key in the effect-side selector language (`selector_keys`), naming the permanent this Aura or Equipment is currently attached to, so a triggered or activated ability can operate on the enchanted/equipped creature: `{"op": "add_counters", "objects": {"attached": true}, ...}`. It must also compose with the other selector keys so an `if`/`exists` condition can ask about that creature's printed or derived characteristics -- `{"exists": {"attached": true, "subtypes": ["Vampire"]}}` for the Vampire clause -- and it must resolve to nothing when the source is unattached, so the trigger is a no-op rather than an error while the Equipment sits on the battlefield alone
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `attached` exists today only in `static_filter_keys`: `characteristics.py` reads `selector.get("attached")` against `source.attached_to` when applying a *continuous* effect, which is why "Equipped creature gets +1/+0 and has flying" works, but `SELECTOR_KEYS` in `engine/effects/selectors.py` has no such key, so no `op` can reach the attached creature. `binding` and `exclude_binding` name what a trigger bound -- here the creature that died, not the equipped one -- and the `creature_dies` event carries no attachment binding. `target` would make the counters a targeted choice the printed line does not offer and would also let the ability be put on the stack pointing at a creature the Equipment is not on. `self_only` names the Equipment itself. Every Equipment currently in the pool has only static abilities plus the `attach` equip ability, so nothing exercises this path yet.
